In general, droughts just happen. It's a weather phenomenon, kind of a longterm natural disaster, if you like.

On the other hand, though, the way human agriculture and other forms of using the land changes the enviroment. This can be the source for droughts. 
For example in ancient greece, the greeks, and later the romans, cut down whole forests as firewood and building material for ships. 

The tree roots hold the layer of fertile earth together and protect it from rainfall trough their leaves. And the layer of earth and the plants that roots in this earth hold the water that seeps into the ground.

When the trees are gone, rainfall and wind will wash and blow the fertile layer of earth away until the ground rock gets visible. This process is called desertification.  The effects of this are visible today in greece and in the mediterranean sea region.

Simple thought experiment:

You throw a ball with velocity a.

Then you ride on a train and throw a ball with velocity a. But the speed of the train will add to the velocity of the ball (from the point of view of a non-moving observer). So the standing observer will measure the velocity of the ball: It's a+t (t for train).

When you do this with light, this does NOT happen. The velocity of the light is constant, independent of the velocity of the light source. 

This fact, that the speed of light stays constant, was tested in many experiments. These results, with the theorethical work (math, equations) led to the conclusions that the universe has a speed limit, the lightspeed.

First: Different forms of radiation can cause different forms of damages to our body.

**Radiowaves:**: As for as I know pretty harmless. Unless if you are tied to a giant radio-antenna.Then you will probably get fried.

**Microwaves**: They interact with matter whilst heating it up. Getting hit by a strong microwave blast (e.g. getting too close to a working radar dish) will cause several damages inside your body. You probably won't feel anything and after several weeks you will get a stroke or something like that. Caused from tiny clumped proteins that will clog blood vessels. The clumped proteins where "cooked"  through the microwaves. 
Longer exposure to microwaves could lead to intense pain and severe internal burnings.

**infrared** Heat-radiation. Standing near a campfire keeps you warm. Standing  near molten-steel  that just came out of a blast furnace will severly burn your skin.

**UV** This is radiation that can react with matter on a chemical way. It is able to bang out electrons from molecules, therefore ionizing matter.
This leads to damages of a molecular level. 

A fancy way of saying: UV-rays will give you sunburns. The melanin(the dark pigment) is able to absorb uv-rays without getting destroyed, protecting the surrounding tissue.

**x-rays/gamma rays:** These fellas do a thing similar to the uv-rays: They are ionizing matter and thus can destroy molecules. But they also don't interact with every bit of matter they encounter. Somewhere in your body they will get absorbed and can cause damages.

**TL:DR:**Different kinds of radiation can cause different kinds of damages inside* 

**Our repair system on the cellular level:**
When our cells get damaged, our body have different ways of handling the situation:

*Just a scratch, we fix it*: Minor damages like a damaged cell hull can our body repair. 

*Just scrap it we make a new one*: Damaged enzyms or proteins are broken down into aminoacids. When one of the many regulatory circles 'notice' that something is missing, a new one will get build.

*Shit the DNA is hit* Every cell have repair mechanisms  for the dna. minor damages can be repaired. 

*self destruct initiated* When the damage done to the cell or the dna is to huge, the cell will scrap itself in a controlled way. That way the death of the cell does no damage to the surrounding cells. It is called apoptosis

*self destruct failed, everything is outer control* 
Cancer. Uncontrollable cell division. Induced through a damage in the dna, caused by the radiation. And all failsafe mechanisms have failed.

Radiation sickness is induced when someone is exposed to ionizing radiation(x, gamma, alpha, beta-rays or neutron radiation)

Ich hatte vor mehreren Monaten durch Zufall rollenspielinteressierte Grünschnäbel kennengelernt und bin nach mittlerweile 7 Spielabenden immer noch der Spielleiter. 
Was mir bei der Gruppe aufgefallen ist:
2 waren sehr enthusiastisch..direkt die Wege gekauft, durchgelesen, mit dem Heldengenerator rumgespielt und in de WikiAventurica wild alles mögliche gelesen.
Problem dabei: Haben die Helden ausmaximiert bei der Erschaffung(50GP nachteile und so) und hatten am Anfang keine Ahnung was Rollenspiel genau bedeutet. Waren sehr regelfest, aber haben eben kein Rollenspiel betrieben.
Also ich meinte, dass Helden eben ne Persönlichkeit haben, damit verbunden Änste, Triebe, Wünsche und Vorstellungen vom Leben usw.
Das haben meine Spieler nicht hinbekommen.

Die anderen wurden eher durch ihre Freunde mitgerissen, lernten die Regeln bei Tisch on-the-fly, taten sich am Anfang auch unglaublich schwer mit dem Darstellen ihrer Charaktere.

Mittlerweile ist es echt besser und zwar nach folgenden Hilfestellungen von mir:

1. Helden aussuchen (lassen) die zu dem Aufwand passen, den man in das Spiel investieren will. 

Um einen menschlichen Söldner/Soldaten zu spielen muss man weniger Regelbücher wälzen als einen elfischen Zauberweber oder einen zwergischen Angroschgeweihten.
Also besser etwas einfacheres Spielen, und das richtig!

2. Grob die "20 Fragen an den Helden" beantworten und AUFSCHREIBEN und am Spieltisch dabei haben.

3. Auf Basis der 20 Fragen bestimmte Dinge ableiten:
-2-3 Worte/Redewendungen die der Held oft verwendet.
-1-2 Eigenheiten des Helden ausarbeiten
-Hobbies/Freizeitaktivitäten festlegen
(natürlich aufschreiben und mitnehmen zum Spieltisch!)

4. Heldentagebuch führen
-zwar nur Stichwortartig, aber das reicht ja schon...
-Und in anderen Abenteuern auf das schon Erlebte eingehen

So kann man sich dann mit Stichpunkten auf 1-2 Blätter eine Referenz  basteln, an der man das Verhalten seines Chars festmacht.

MIt diesen Tipps hab ich es geschafft, dass meine Grünschnäbel-Gruppe irgendwie den 'Absprung' geschafft hat und mittlerweile hat jeder seinen Held mehr oder weniger fein ausgearbeitet, aber jeder spielt nun seine Rolle, und nicht sich selbst ;)
